advancedHtml.frontHtml:
Unit circle · special angles

A point at angle θ on the unit circle is (cos θ, sin θ). Give the coordinates at 0°, 30°, 45°, 60°, 90°.

Read cos as the x-coordinate and sin as the y-coordinate.
advancedHtml.backHtml:
Unit circle · special angles

A point at angle θ on the unit circle is (cos θ, sin θ). Give the coordinates at 0°, 30°, 45°, 60°, 90°.

x-coordinate = cos θ, y-coordinate = sin θ. Values: 30° → (√3/2, ½); 45° → (1/√2, 1/√2); 60° → (½, √3/2).

Memory: sin goes 0, ½, 1/√2, √3/2, 1 (write as √0/2, √1/2, √2/2, √3/2, √4/2); cos runs the same list backwards.

cards.term: The sine wave is the height of a point moving round the unit circle
cards.definition: sin θ is the height of the point at angle θ on the unit circle; plotting height against θ gives the sine wave with period 2π, range [−1,1]

advancedHtml.frontHtml:
Sine graph from the unit circle

How does the sine curve come from the unit circle? Follow the height of a point as θ goes from 0 to 2π.

Track only the vertical position.
advancedHtml.backHtml:
Sine graph from the unit circle

How does the sine curve come from the unit circle? Follow the height of a point as θ goes from 0 to 2π.

The height of the point at angle θ is sin θ. Carry each height across to the matching θ on the horizontal axis and join the dots: the sine wave.

One turn of the circle = one period 2π; max 1 at π/2, min −1 at 3π/2; zeros at 0, π, 2π. Cosine is the same wave started a quarter-turn earlier.

Trap: is sin(A + B) = sin A + sin B?
cards.definition: No. sin 90° = 1 but sin 45° + sin 45° = √2. Sine is not linear: use sin A cos B + cos A sin B

cards.term: Trap: sin²x is (sin x)², but sin x² means?
cards.definition: sin(x²). Also sin⁻¹x is the inverse function, not 1/sin x (that is cosec x)

cards.term: If A + B + C = π, then tan A + tan B + tan C = ?
cards.definition: tan A tan B tan C. Because tan(A + B) = −tan C. Also cot A cot B + cot B cot C + cot C cot A = 1

cards.term: If A + B + C = π: sin 2A + sin 2B + sin 2C = ? and cos A + cos B + cos C = ?
cards.definition: 4 sin A sin B sin C and 1 + 4 sin(A/2) sin(B/2) sin(C/2)

Multiply by cos 60° = ½: 1/16

cards.definition:
Multiply by 2 sin(x/2) and use 2 sin(x/2) cos kx = sin((k + ½)x) − sin((k − ½)x).
The terms telescope to
sin(nx/2) cos((n + 1)x/2) / sin(x/2)

cards.term: Value of sin 18° via a quick derivation (idea).
cards.definition: Let θ = 18°: 5θ = 90° so sin 2θ = cos 3θ → 2 sin θ cos θ = 4cos³θ − 3 cos θ → 4 sin²θ + 2 sin θ − 1 = 0 → sin 18° = (√5 − 1)/4

Solving sin x = ½

Solve sin x = ½ on the unit circle. What is the general solution?

Where is the y-coordinate equal to ½?
advancedHtml.backHtml:
Solving sin x = ½

Solve sin x = ½ on the unit circle. What is the general solution?

sin x = y-coordinate = ½: the horizontal line y = ½ meets the circle at 30° and 150° (π − π/6).

Adding full turns: x = 2nπ + π/6 or 2nπ + 5π/6, combined as x = nπ + (−1)ⁿ π/6 (n ∈ Z).

cards.definition: sin x = 0: x = nπ; cos x = 0: x = (2n + 1)π/2; tan x = 0: x = nπ; sin x = sin α: x = nπ + (−1)ⁿ α; cos x = cos α: x = 2nπ ± α; tan x = tan α: x = nπ + α; sin²x = sin²α: x = nπ ± α

advancedHtml.frontHtml:
General solutions

sin x = 0?
cos x = 0?
tan x = 0?
sin x = sin α?
cos x = cos α?
tan x = tan α?
sin²x = sin²α?
advancedHtml.backHtml:
General solutions

Write the general solution (n ∈ Z).

sin x = 0x = nπ
cos x = 0x = (2n + 1)π/2
tan x = 0x = nπ
sin x = sin αx = nπ + (−1)ⁿ α
cos x = cos αx = 2nπ ± α
tan x = tan αx = nπ + α
sin²x = sin²αx = nπ ± α

cards.definition: (2 sin x − 1)(sin x + 1) = 0 → sin x = ½ → x = nπ + (−1)ⁿπ/6; or sin x = −1 → x = 2nπ − π/2

cards.term: Solve tan x = √3 and sin x = −1/2 in [0, 2π).

cards.definition: Divide by √2: sin(x + π/4) = 1/√2 → x + π/4 = nπ + (−1)ⁿπ/4 → x = 2nπ or x = 2nπ + π/2

cards.term: Trap: solving sin x cos x = sin x by dividing by sin x.
cards.definition:
You lose the roots of sin x = 0.
Factorise instead: sin x (cos x − 1) = 0
→ x = nπ or x = 2nπ, so x = nπ overall

1) Reduce to one function (identities).
2) Factorise (never cancel a factor that can be 0).
3) Use the general solution formulas.
4) Restrict to the required interval by choosing integer n

cards.term: Number of real solutions of sin x = x/10?
cards.definition: The graphs y = sin x and y = x/10 can meet only for |x| ≤ 10: 3 crossings for x > 0, 3 for x < 0 and x = 0, so 7
